rules.statement: After a successful interactive sign-in, redirect only to a ReturnUrl that has been validated as a local URL; never redirect to an unvalidated caller-supplied return URL.
rules.why: The login endpoint honors a server-validated ReturnUrl as an open-redirect guard.
rules.check: Look for login/sign-in handlers that call Redirect(returnUrl) or Results.Redirect with a query/form value without a local-URL check (e.g. Url.IsLocalUrl or equivalent).

rules.statement: Interactive login must verify credentials through the existing local-account credential verification seam rather than introducing a second credential verifier.
rules.why: The local-account store already owns credentials; a parallel verifier duplicates and diverges credential checks.
rules.check: Flag new password/credential comparison logic in login endpoints that bypasses the shared credential verification interface used by other grants.

rules.statement: Serve the interactive login/consent surface from the same origin as the OpenID Provider that issues the session cookie, and submit its forms as native HTML form POSTs rather than fetch/XHR.
rules.why: The cookie LoginPath redirect, antiforgery-protected POST, Set-Cookie and ReturnUrl round-trip only work cleanly same-origin, and native POSTs let the browser (and Selenium) follow the Set-Cookie plus redirect.
rules.check: Look for login/consent pages hosted on a separate origin (dev server, CDN) or login/consent submissions implemented with fetch/axios instead of a <form method="post">.

rules.statement: Set the stable conformance locator ids (username, password, login, consent-allow, consent-deny) explicitly on login/consent form elements instead of relying on UI-library-generated ids.
rules.why: Conformance browser automation locates fields by stable id/name, and generated ids (e.g. MUI's) are not stable selectors; the ids are a maintenance invariant coupled to the conformance browser config.
rules.check: In login/consent components, verify the inputs and buttons carry explicit id/name attributes matching the locator contract; flag renames or removal without a matching conformance config update.

rules.statement: Make the interactive authentication module (cookie scheme and login/consent endpoints) an explicit opt-in registration that the host calls, never wired by default.
rules.why: The interactive surface is a first-class opt-in capability; hosts opt in with one call.
rules.check: Flag default service registration or middleware setup that implicitly registers the interactive cookie scheme or maps login/consent endpoints without the host opting in.

rules.statement: Seed browser SPA clients as public clients (empty secret set, PKCE required, explicit redirect_uris), idempotently through the normal persistence/seeding path.
rules.why: SPA clients cannot hold secrets, and seeding through the normal persistence path on the tenant seed fan-out keeps provisioning consistent and repeatable.
rules.check: Look for seeded SPA clients that carry secrets, lack PKCE enforcement or redirect_uris, or are inserted by bypassing the standard seeding pipeline or non-idempotently.
